name: Possibility Playground at Hayswood Park
summary: One of the largest inclusive playgrounds in the Midwest, designed with Playcraft Systems.
paragraphs: Hayswood Nature Reserve has long been the crown jewel of Harrison County Parks. For decades the playground sitting on the Persimmon Ridge overlooking Indian Creek was an exciting playground stop for kids from all over the surrounding counties. Oftentimes school field trips from all over the area come to Corydon, IN for the historical aspect of it being the first capital of Indiana. While in town, they would often find themselves picnicking at the playground or visiting a realistic reenactment of the Battle of Corydon.

In December of 2019, a call came into the CRG office for an interview with Harrison County Parks Director Larry Shickles and Harrison County Prosecutor Otto Schalk to discuss a new playground project that would change the landscape of not only Hayswood Park, but the vision of what an inclusive playground can look like going forward. This interview was to narrow down the possibilities for which companies would provide the three proposals from a pool of about 12 suppliers. After the initial discussions, CRG was chosen as one of the three providers.

Once the decision was made about who to work with, the discussion turned to just how big this area would be and what it would entail… It was at this point that Mr. Shickles said something along the lines of “We want the biggest and grandest inclusive playground in the Midwest!” Let the work begin.

With that information at hand, CRG began working directly with Playcraft Systems to design the most inclusive and action-packed playground ever built. Spanning nearly 300 feet in length and nearly 150 feet wide in some areas, the new designs were approximately the size of a football field. With dozens of accessible play panels, nearly 20 slides, hundreds of linear feet of accessible ramps and decks, climbing nets, tall towers, enough climbing equipment to keep kids busy finding new events all day long, and with fully accessible surfacing, the three options put together for the board presentation were sure to impress.

Many discussions were had regarding what to name this place. There were many good ones, but “The Possibility Playground at Hayswood Park” was the only name fitting for something this big. The possibilities are nearly endless!

After many months of installation, the new playground was opened to the public on October 22nd, 2023. Three days of festivities, state dignitaries, and celebration welcomed this new playground to the world. As one of the largest playgrounds on the planet, it was our humble honor to have been a vital part of making it a reality. We look forward to years of stories from those at Harrison County Parks.

quotes.text: When we started the five-year journey to building the Possibility Playground we looked extensively at several companies to design and install this new playground. After two rounds of interviews and deliberation it was clear that the folks at Commercial Recreation Group seemed fit to serve us best on this unique venture. What we found was that Commercial Recreation Group quickly became our partner and not just the vendor. Through the whole process the entire team at Commercial Recreation Group was there to work and guide us. Possibility Playground has been a wonderful success and it truly could not have been such a success without the CRG folks on our team and since the project is over they are still there every step of the way.
quotes.name: Larry Shickles

photo_alt: Aerial view of the large Possibility Playground at Hayswood Park: multiple green and blue play structures with shade sails on blue and green poured-in-place surfacing, a swing area in front and picnic tables on a concrete pad.

name: Cool Creek Park
summary: Hamilton County’s feature playground: 20-foot towers, shade sails, musical play and adult fitness.
paragraphs: Cool Creek Park playground is the feature playground in the Hamilton County Parks Department lineup. Designing a playground for such a well known and respected park department was a tall feat that we gladly took on. It was a pleasure and an honor to be able to provide our design and equipment for this project. It was featured in the [July-October 2019 issue](https://www.hamiltoncounty.in.gov/DocumentCenter/View/847/New-Chatterbox-Leisure-Guide-PDF?bidId=) of Hamilton County Parks & Recreation publication _The Chatterbox._

The new Cool Creek Playground was designed with the outgoing playground layout in mind. That said, the park board asked that we implement a new concept that the park department is looking to include in many of the parks around Hamilton County, called SOMAstations. This is a social interaction focused adult fitness area, that we specifically placed so that parents can keep an eye on their kids of either age group while working on that physique.

The play structures were designed to optimize play value and interaction throughout the entire structure. The many slides, climbers and ladders promote kids having to navigate their way to the top of the over 20 foot tall structure to then slide back down. To literally top things off, the structures are fitted with multi-colored 12' wide shade sails that provide ample shade for those hot summer days spent on the playground.

Large, colorful musical pieces were added to the design to be sure everyone can have fun. These include a line of 9 foot tall musical chimes that can be played by using attached mallets. Five multi-colored drums and 4 large musical flowers round out the list.

Lastly, multiple styles of swings were chosen to give visitors of all abilities the thrill a playground is meant to provide. The list includes 2 large disc swings, 2 ADA inclusive swings, 6 standard belt seats, 1 toddler seat, and a new product by Playcraft Systems, the Playshare swing. This is a 2 seat swing with an adult seat on one side and a toddler bucket on the other, so parent and baby can enjoy swinging together.

quotes.text: On a “playful” note, we are so excited about our new playground at Cool Creek Park…The proposal submitted by Hamilton County’s own, [Commercial Recreation Group], was outstanding! The highly-regarded Noblesville firm went head-to-head with some of the nation’s largest playground companies and outclassed them with their proposal.
quotes.name: Allen Patterson

name: Hargan Matthews Park
summary: A fully accessible steamboat playground on the Ohio River.
paragraphs: The City of Madison approached CRG in 2014 about renovating a local park. After several visits and learning about the history of their beautiful city, we were so excited to be a part of this project.
The park sits on the north side of the Ohio River and is in the heart of the city. Their initial vision was a ‘steamboat’ play structure, and has since evolved into so much more.

The project was to be geared towards children of all abilities, including those who use wheelchairs, so it was important to include full ADA ramp accessibility. Poured-in-place surfacing mixed with artificial turf brings the entire playground to life as the ‘boat’ actually sits in the blue surfacing and is floating down the river.

quotes.text: Commercial Recreation Group help us create an accessible playground for the children of our community. It took us four years to raise the money. They worked with use well through the entire process. We appreciate all of their help in making this dream a reality.

summary: Two pavilions joined by a metal pergola at Coxhall Gardens.
paragraphs: We were contracted by Myers Construction, a local general contractor who has worked on many park projects, to supply the shade structure aspect of this project. This Americana structure consists of two pavilions which are connected by a metal pergola. Several meetings went into finalizing this specific design and the end product speaks for itself!

name: Burris Laboratory School
summary: One of the largest composite playground structures in the nation.
paragraphs: Every once in a while a project comes along that transcends the stereotypical playground improvement. When a community sees a playground as part of their childhood, and a part of the community itself, extra care and consideration is required. This was the case with the school playground, “Burris Backyard” at the Burris Laboratory School in Muncie, Indiana. Originally a large community involvement project to build a massive wood structure that has stood as a symbol of pride for an amazing 20 years, time had taken its toll, and a replacement was needed.

Though we were chosen to handle the project, fine tuning the details of the final structure was a long process between Shane Burris, our project manager, the architects from Ball State University, and the fine executive staff at Burris Lab School. Together, we had designed what would be one of the largest composite playground structures in the nation.

The time had come for the work to begin. Removal of the iconic wood structure was the talk of the neighborhood, including ridicule from many of those involved with the original project many years ago. As the construction of the new structure continued, interest turned to excitement. The massive structure rose from the ground and began to transform into a vision that many believed would never return to the Backyard.

Once completed, it was obvious that the new playground not only met, but exceeded the expectations set forth by those with such fond memories of the past. With the fine products produced by Playcraft Systems, this will be a structure that stands the test of time for the next 20 plus years of play for generations of kids that visit or attend this amazing school.
It was our distinct honor and pleasure to be affiliated with a truly memorable project such as the “Burris Backyard” project at the Burris Laboratory School.

name: Asa Bales Park
summary: A Ninja Warrior-style parkour playground, chosen by local students.
paragraphs: The truly unique aspect of Asa Bales Park has nothing to do with the equipment, installation, or even the finished product. The great folks at the Parks Department for the City of Westfield decided early on that the final decision must lie in the hands of those whose opinions count the most. After narrowing the pool of 10 design entries down to 3, the final 3 were shared with the Westfield Middle School Student Council. This group of students were then responsible for making the final decision to go with the design submitted by Commercial Recreation Group.

Asa Bales Park includes a parkour design that was to mimic a “Ninja Warrior” type of layout. The structure itself is not the typical “slides and climbers” type of playground. Rope features, ladder obstacles, and step pods are side features to the 13 foot tall main hub of nets in the center that bring it all together. Multiple types of overhead and ground level features make this playground the ultimate obstacle course for the 5-12 year old age group and beyond. That is what makes this playground special.

The surfacing chosen for this project is a new design of turf that incorporates a CPSC certified cushion under a tough, realistic grass turf that is not only designed to stand the test of time, but look great in the process. This was all wrapped in a concrete curb to keep everything in place.

name: Boys & Girls Club of Noblesville
summary: A new playground and gym scoreboards for the club’s new building.
paragraphs: Commercial Recreation Group recently completed a new playset for the Boys and Girls Club here in Noblesville. The Boys and Girls Club provides positive and engaging programs that enrich the lives of a diverse group of members ranging in age from kindergarten through 12th grade. When they moved to a new, larger building to serve a growing number of youth, naturally they needed a new playground! That’s where we came in. Their younger guests now have a fun and exciting playground to help burn off all that extra energy. We also provided two new scoreboards for their gymnasium.

name: Lake Forest Neighborhood
summary: A fully ADA-compliant neighborhood playground.
paragraphs: At Commercial Recreation Group, we believe that play time is essential to the well being of all youngsters, regardless of physical limitations. This is why we offer a wide variety of ADA compliant play structures, ramps, and surfacing. Our commercial division recently had the opportunity to construct a fully ADA compliant playground in Noblesville, IN. This new playground structure is wheelchair accessible and features wood mulch and timbers for an aesthetically pleasing, natural look. We completed the sidewalks for this project as well.

If you’re interested in learning more about ADA compliance, and would like to make sure your commercial playground is up to current standards, give us a call at [(317) 776-7830](tel:+13177767830). We’d love to help you ensure quality play time for everyone.

name: Thomas A. Hendricks Elementary School
summary: A new school playground in green and yellow, built in 10 days.
paragraphs: We recently finished a brand new playground for Thomas A. Hendricks Elementary School in Shelbyville, IN. The budget for the project was $85k and it was completed in 10 days. The play area is designed for children aged 5-12 and is complete with swings, awesome climbers, and a main play structure in their eye-catching school colors of green and yellow.

name: The Play School at Legacy
summary: Pirate ship and island play on custom poured-in-place surfacing.
paragraphs: Our commercial division just finished an awesome project for The Play School at Legacy in Carmel, Indiana. The Legacy school is a brand new location for The Play School with a state of the art interior space and now a wonderful outdoor play area.

The structures include a pirate boat theme and an island theme. The main play set is a blue and red pirate ship design from Playcraft Systems. It hosts features such as double curved slides, a climbing rock wall, rock steps, and double traversing rings.

This project featured poured-in-place safety surfacing, which is a rubber surface that can be customized to different colors, designs, and shapes. It’s high quality surfacing that protects and lasts through years of use. It has a light, springy feel when stepped on and is extremely safe for children at play. This poured-in-place design is made to look like the pirate boat is in the water and the second structure is on an island with sand and a shore line. It feels like you’re on an island, and makes it easy for children to let their imaginations work while playing.

The project was finished exactly as the rendering showed. Our commercial team provides these renderings for every new project we take on. This rendering gave The Play School a perfect visual idea of what their new playground would look like before the project even began.
This project was completed in roughly 14 days from start to finish.

quotes.text: We had so much fun taking our school’s aquatic theme and extending it to our outdoor playground and building a creative, eye catching, fun and safe play space!… We look forward to the next opportunity to work together to build another Play School playground. We just can’t THANK YOU enough for building us the most incredible playground for the children of The Play School at Legacy! You were absolutely the best, most professional vendor we have ever worked with… You spent significant time learning our business and listening to our needs. It was clear from the start that you knew all the age and equipment laws and regulations, and you helped us meet the stringent child care licensing rules in our industry.
quotes.name: Katie Guerra

photo_alt: Blue and red pirate-ship play structure with two children hanging from overhead rings, a tan rock-climbing tower at right, on blue poured-in-place rubber surfacing beside a school building.

name: Meridian Health Services
summary: A nature-themed playground for toddlers through age 12.
paragraphs: We completed an exciting playground project for the Susan Gresham Center at Meridian Health Services in Muncie, Indiana.

This playground has a lot of different features. The tree toppers on the playground structure give it a nature type of feel along with all of the green & brown colors. Some features of the structure include a spiral slide, net climber & a rock wall. There is also a row of ground level panels next to the structure which can be utilized by children in wheelchairs. The customer wanted this playground to be for toddlers all the way up to 12 year olds, so we installed a toddler climbing structure on top of poured-in-place rubber surfacing.

Most of the surfacing for this playground is our Engineered Hardwood Playground Mulch but we did install a small pad of our Poured-in-Place rubber surfacing. We installed the PIP underneath the toddler climbing structure. The playground is also bordered with our 12" tall black plastic timbers. We installed this playground ‘below grade’ so that the top of the timbers would be flush with the grass.

quotes.text: We had as much fun working on the project with the folks at [Commercial Recreation Group] as the kids are now having on the playground itself! Travis was with us every step of the way, helping two departments that had never worked together collaborate and develop a custom design that made everyone happy. Timelines were developed, deadlines were met, and budgets were hit. Communication was thorough throughout. But most importantly, on the day of our ribbon cutting our donors were thrilled! I know we’ll be doing more ‘work’ (if you can call it that) with Commercial Recreation Group.
quotes.name: Meridian Health Services

name: Kokomo Jackrabbits
summary: A baseball-themed play structure at Kokomo Municipal Stadium.
paragraphs: The Kokomo Jackrabbits are a collegiate summer league team and a member of the summer collegiate Prospect League. The [Jackrabbits](https://www.kokomojackrabbits.com/) play at the 4,000-seat Kokomo Municipal Stadium in downtown Kokomo, Indiana. Our commercial division was challenged with creating a modern play structure based on America’s pastime. The result was pretty spectacular!

Look closely at the play structure, and you’ll see steel baseball cap roofs on each tower. The baseball-themed structure provides the perfect backdrop to the stadium. This hybrid structure features 6 slides, a burma bridge, vertical rock climber, tic-tac-toe panel, lily-pad step-up, and many climbing devices. Next to the main structure also sits a tri-pad jungle traverse with climbing elements. This structure is rated for children in the 5-12 year age range.

This project incorporated blue rubber mulch safety surfacing, which cushions falls and minimizes dangerous playground impacts. It’s high quality surfacing that protects and lasts through years of use. It has a light, springy feel when stepped on and eliminates the need for annual mulching, since rubber doesn’t break down as wood does. The blue provides a nice visual color to catch your eye and match the play structure. The surfacing is contained with functional border timbers that help keep the rubber mulch in place during heavy traffic. They also provide a nice border for the play area.

quotes.text: Working with Travis from Commercial Recreation Group was a great experience. From the design phase to the installation, he was there helping us through every inch of the way. Even though we had a very tight schedule, he was also able to meet our completion date.
quotes.name: Randy Morris

name: Yorktown Elementary School
summary: A new play structure and 8-person swing frame for grades 3–5.
paragraphs: Yorktown Elementary is situated in downtown Yorktown, Indiana right off IN-32 (about 10 minutes outside of Muncie). Our commercial division tackled designing and installing an updated play structure just East of the school.

This structure features 4 slides (spiral & triple twister slide), a curved erector rock climber, observation deck, 360 degree horizontal ladder, slider & disc traverse, tic-tac-toe panel, and many climbing devices. Accompanying the main structure is an 8-person swing frame. This structure is rated for children 5-12 years of age.

This project incorporated engineered [wood fiber](products.html#safety-surfacing) safety surfacing, which is non-toxic, has no contaminants, or heavy metals. It’s probably the most common playground surfacing solution. The surfacing is contained with functional border timbers that help keep the wood fiber mulch in place during heavy traffic. They also provide a nice border for the play area.

quotes.text: Working with Travis Goebel and [Commercial Recreation Group] was a fantastic experience for Yorktown Elementary School. Travis listened to the needs and wants of the students and created an engaging and age appropriate play area for our 3rd-5th grade students. He was aware that the playground would need to be purchased in two phases due to funding and designed the area for easy equipment additions. Overall, the design and installation process was stress-free and fun for Yorktown Elementary students. The students LOVE their new playground!
quotes.name: Heather Lucas

name: Town of Buffalo
summary: A new town play park with two large structures and nine slides.
paragraphs: We took on this massive project for the town of Buffalo, Indiana. This new play park was built next to the local baseball field and would serve as an iconic point in the community. The project took our division 15 days to complete.

There are two large play structures and many smaller structures that make up this play structure. There are 9 slides in total! Included are a triple twister, dual express, wave slide, and (2) two spiral tube slides. The side-by-side curly tube slides give the main play structure a unique geometric look. The colors are bold and playful.

This project incorporated engineered [wood fiber](products.html#safety-surfacing) safety surfacing, which is non-toxic, has no contaminants, or heavy metals. It’s probably the most common playground surfacing solution. The surfacing is contained with functional border timbers that help keep the wood fiber mulch in place during heavy traffic. They also provide a nice border for the play area.

quotes.text: In the process of constructing a new park system in the town of Buffalo, we looked at a lot of play ground equipment vendors. We selected [Commercial Recreation Group] for their expertise, service, quality, product choice, and availability. Travis Goebel and all the folks at [Commercial Recreation Group] are very professional, knowledgeable and courteous. [Commercial Recreation Group] made the whole process very easy from the first thought to planning, and construction.
quotes.name: Mike McCormick

name: The Westons
summary: A new HOA playground, swings and cantilever shade over the pool.
paragraphs: Recently, the HOA president of the Westons neighborhood (located in Carmel, Indiana near the intersection of N. Michigan Road and West 106th Street) reached out to us to inquire about a new playground. We met with the HOA board to show them a variety of options that would fit the needs of their community.

After final structures and layouts were chosen, work on the new play area began. We removed the entire existing structure, including the old wood mulch that would be replaced with rubber mulch. Then, installation of new equipment began. We installed a Playcraft Hybrid play structure, 2 bays of swings, timbers, and rubber mulch. We then added 2 large cantilever shade structures over the pool area. We finished the project with a few benches and trash receptacles. Despite a few rain delays, the entire project was completed in two weeks, and the community now has a new and improved area to relax, connect, and play.

name: Brownstown Pavilion
summary: A new pavilion with a wheelchair access ramp.
paragraphs: We created and installed this beautiful new pavilion for the city of Brownstown, Indiana. The structure, complete with wheelchair access ramp was completed in two weeks with a budget of $80k.

name: Mall of America
summary: Poured-in-place surfacing for a Paw Patrol themed play area.
paragraphs: Mall of America is known for being a source of wonder and excitement for children of all ages. And since CRG is all about fun, we were of course thrilled to be part of a larger project that will provide Mall of America’s youngest guests with even more opportunity for adventure.

Commercial Recreation Group had the pleasure of (quite literally) laying the foundation for this incredible Paw Patrol themed play area. The surface was completed using poured-in-place rubber, an extremely durable material that can be fully customized to any design or color scheme. If you happen to be in the Minneapolis area, be sure to stop by the Mall of America to see the finished product!

name: Home Gym
summary: Commercial-grade basketball goals and wall padding for a home gym.
paragraphs: Commercial Recreation Group completed a beautiful new home gym for a customer in Westfield, IN. The customer was looking for two basketball units and padding for the entire room. We provided them with a main commercial grade wall mount goal that is height adjustable and a shooting station designed for children. We also installed commercial grade wall padding that is 6' tall and 2" thick.

2' x 6' Bonded Wall Pad – Nail Lip Attachment

name: Pipe Creek Elementary
summary: A shade structure for a play area with no trees.
paragraphs: This project was for a school that was looking for an area for kids to play when the temperature rises. They had no shade or trees in the area, so a new shade structure was the perfect solution. With this model, we were able to keep a free and clear area while providing shade.

name: Edgewood Elementary School
summary: 28,000 square feet of poured-in-place surfacing with new drainage.
paragraphs: Commercial Recreation Group was contracted to install new poured-in-place rubber surfacing at Edgewood Elementary in Ellettsville, IN. The project included removing approximately 1,700 cubic yards of existing wood fiber playground mulch before installing 600 linear feet of sub surface drainage tile, 1,200 linear feet of concrete curbing, 2,500 tons of compacted stone sub-base, 28,000 square feet of poured-in-place surfacing & 17,000 sq ft of rubber playground mulch. Wow! Needless to say, the result is an outstanding new surface that has given the existing play structures renewed life.

Poured-in-place surfacing was an ideal choice for Edgewood Elementary because of its durability, fully customizable design, and ADA friendliness. The children at Edgewood Elementary can now enjoy their new-and-improved play experience thanks to the surfacing makeover!

name: City of Fort Wayne
summary: New playgrounds at Klug, Reservoir and Hamilton parks.
paragraphs: Commercial Recreation Group had the privilege of providing and installing new playground equipment for three locations in the Fort Wayne, IN area: Klug Park, Reservoir Park, and Hamilton Park. We were contracted to remove existing equipment that had been in place for 15-20 years before installing new equipment. The old structures were out of code and in need of replacement. Enter: Commercial Recreation Group! We installed new playground structures suitable for ages 2-5 and 5-12 to provide everyone with a safe and fun play environment.

Check out the before and after photos to see the incredible transformations. We’d like to thank the Fort Wayne Parks and Rec department for the opportunity to provide playgrounds for the community that will be enjoyed by children for many years to come.

name: Westport Homes Gazebo
summary: A waterfront gazebo for Westport Homes.
paragraphs: We do much more than just playgrounds. This beautiful waterfront gazebo completed for Westport Homes is one of our favorites. Its location provided some unique challenges and the results showcase just how we were able to meet those challenges to produce the final product.
